summary: Restore the bird as the object of “im Käfig” and correct two typos
before: auf den Tisch gelegt und im Kägif (eingeserrt)
after: auf den Tisch gelegt und den Vogel im Käfig (eingesperrt)
rationale: The supplied translation of 21/34 explicitly distinguishes the apples placed on the table from “den Vogel im Käfig (eingesperrt)”. The entry drops “den Vogel”, making the apples the object of both descriptions. “Kägif” and “eingeserrt” are also evident typos.

summary: File the cattle-taking example under sense 1
rationale: Sense 2 means depriving someone of their reason (məx diḏ-). Both the Turoyo cattle object aq qanyonayḏan and the supplied English “stole all our cattle” describe taking away, covered by sense 1, not loss of reason.

summary: Remove the bringing example from the marriage sense
rationale: The example uses kǝbli/komawbli with an object and a destination l ruḥayye; its supplied translation describes bringing and spreading accusations. It does not concern marriage. Sense 1 already covers taking/bringing, as illustrated by the food-bringing example ybl.III.t.preterit.1. This reclassification does not resolve or alter the figurative English translation.

summary: File taking people into the army under sense 1
rationale: The government takes people into military service (an noše li ʕaskariye; supplied translation “drafts the people into the army”). This belongs to taking/bringing in sense 1, not “heiraten” in sense 3.

summary: Move “Sergey and” from the Turoyo field to the English translation
before: Lu Sargey w li Gule aq qanyonayḏan kulle blǝnne/mballe. ‘’Sergey and
after: Lu Sargey w li Gule aq qanyonayḏan kulle blǝnne/mballe.

data.translation: Sergey and Gule stole all our cattle.

rationale: The raw example contains the complete English sentence “Sergey and Gule stole all our cattle.” Its beginning and stray quotation marks were left in the Turoyo field, while the translation field starts mid-sentence. Restore the two fields together.

summary: Restore the missing “zu” in “kommen zu können”
before: mit sich um zu ihrem Vater kommen können
after: mit sich, um zu ihrem Vater kommen zu können
rationale: The German purpose clause requires the infinitive “kommen zu können”. This corrects the entry’s grammar without changing its interpretation of ḥatta d-oṯən.
“hicht” is a typo for “nicht”. The source translation has “hören nicht”, and lo=ko-šəmʕi supplies the negation.
The neuter singular collective “Vieh” requires “das ganze Vieh” here; the supplied translation of 75/232 contains this article and the Turoyo has u=ṭarš kule.
The Turoyo abrə-d-u=malko and the supplied translation of 21/73 both identify the king’s son; “Königssehn” is a typo.
The demonstrative/article “den” is ungrammatical here; the supplied translation of 25/14 reads “wer hat denn meine Schale genommen?”.

summary: Correct the masculine possessive in “dein Sohn”
rationale: “Sohn” requires “dein”; the supplied translation of 75/7 also has “dein Sohn”.
The past tense of “sich erklären” is “erklärte”; the umlaut is missing.
After “erklärte sich damit einverstanden”, the subordinate content clause requires the conjunction “dass”.
The noun is missing n; the supplied translation of 57/153 reads “Eigentümer”.
